title: Kubernetes-Native Monitoring Commands
intro: Before Prometheus or Grafana, kubectl itself can answer 'what's slow or erroring right now?'. This is the standard first-five-minutes sequence when a service degrades.

steps.prompt: Check CPU and memory usage per node.
steps.fake_output:
NAME     CPU(cores)  CPU%  MEMORY(bytes)  MEMORY%
node-1   3810m       95%   11012Mi        70%
node-2   410m        10%   5120Mi         32%
steps.explanation: node-1 is nearly maxed on CPU while node-2 is mostly idle.
steps.why: A hot node with an idle neighbor often means poor pod spread — e.g. missing anti-affinity or topology spread constraints letting everything pile onto one node.

steps.prompt: See per-container usage inside each pod, not just per-pod totals.
steps.fake_output:
POD                 NAME        CPU(cores)  MEMORY(bytes)
checkout-7f9d-a1b2  checkout    1890m       610Mi
checkout-7f9d-a1b2  log-agent   12m         40Mi
steps.explanation: The app container itself is the heavy one, not the sidecar.
steps.why: Pod totals hide which container is responsible. With sidecars (log shippers, proxies, service mesh), --containers stops you from blaming the wrong process.

steps.prompt: Pull recent logs from every container in every checkout pod at once.
steps.fake_output:
[checkout-7f9d-a1b2/checkout] level=warn msg="db pool exhausted, waiting"
[checkout-7f9d-c3d4/checkout] level=warn msg="db pool exhausted, waiting"
steps.explanation: Every replica is waiting on the database connection pool.
steps.why: When every replica shows the same symptom, the cause is usually shared — a dependency, not one bad pod. That immediately shifts the investigation from 'which pod' to 'what do they all depend on'.

steps.prompt: Show recent cluster events, newest last, to catch OOM kills, evictions, and failed probes.
steps.fake_output:
LAST SEEN  TYPE     REASON     OBJECT                    MESSAGE
4m         Warning  Unhealthy  pod/checkout-7f9d-a1b2    Readiness probe failed: timeout
1m         Warning  Evicted    pod/report-x9            The node was low on resource: memory
steps.explanation: Readiness failures and a memory eviction.
steps.why: Events expire after about an hour by default — check them early in an incident, or ship them to your log system so they're still there for the post-mortem.

steps.prompt: Pull raw metrics straight from the Kubernetes API server's /metrics endpoint.
steps.explanation: 4120 requests throttled with 429 — something is hammering the API server with LIST calls.
steps.why: Control-plane components expose Prometheus metrics too. A runaway controller or script flooding the API server can slow down the entire cluster, and this is where it shows up.
